<!-- pr-reviewer: d24c20df9e8a99269ae14ddf40e221bb339c1df2 -->
Clean - ready to merge

Independent review of `docs/release-notes-history` @ d24c20d (docs-only; nothing built).

- **Scope:** `gh pr diff 270 --name-only` -> `RELEASE_NOTES.md` only.
- **Additions only:** `git diff --numstat origin/main...` -> `445 0 RELEASE_NOTES.md`; no removed lines.
- **Content (CRLF normalized):** lines 1-83 are byte-identical to `v0.14.0:RELEASE_NOTES.md` (which also equals main's current file); then a blank line, `---`, a blank line; then lines 87-528 are byte-identical to `v0.13.0:RELEASE_NOTES.md` (442 lines, the full history). The only extra bytes compared with a bare concatenation are the two blank lines around `---`. They are needed: without the blank line before it, `---` straight after the paragraph "...until the mouse moves." would render as a setext heading underline and turn that paragraph into an H2.
- **release.yml parse simulated** (the "Release page from the template" step's logic, run in PowerShell on the PR's file): first `---` after TrimEnd is at index 84 (line 85), so `$end > 1`; line 1 is `# CamCraft 0.14.0 (clean-room implementation)`, which matches `0.14.0`; the extracted section is non-empty (4708 chars) and is exactly the 0.14.0 notes without the title. The later `---` lines (85,125,154,...) belong to the 0.13.0 history and come after the cut, so they don't matter.
- **Mergeable:** `gh pr view 270 --json mergeable` -> `MERGEABLE`.

No blockers.

<!-- review-cost: estimated -->
**Estimated agent cost:** ~$1.04 (rough estimate from size: 445 changed lines)

No token usage was recorded for this PR, so this is calibrated from PRs with measured cost (our fix PRs, fix agent + review: median ~$1.20, ~$2.33 per 1,000 changed lines; floor $0.15, cap ~$3.60). For a contributor's PR it estimates what writing and reviewing it the way our agents work would cost, not what their session actually spent.

Blended upper estimate: 90 % input / 10 % output at list price (Opus 5.5 ~$5.60/M, Sonnet 5.5 ~$2.80/M, Haiku 5.5 ~$0.14/M). Cache reads make the real cost lower; main-session coordination isn't counted.
